name: Peregrine Suite
description:
Commissioned in 2219 by the Vantablack Cultural Endowment and released exclusively through Tier 4 and Tier 5 licensed neural feeds, 'Peregrine Suite' is a four-movement AI-assisted composition performed by a seventeen-piece ensemble assembled specifically for this project, led by Maren Solís-Ekwueme, who had spent five years as composer-in-residence at the Spire's Aurantia Concert Hall. The album was composed using a proprietary Vantablack AI system called AXIOM-7 working in collaboration with Solís-Ekwueme's own compositional sketches — the promotional materials are carefully ambiguous about how much of each movement is human-authored and how much is AI-generated, a deliberate aesthetic and commercial choice. The music itself is staggeringly detailed: the first movement, 'Ascent,' draws from Central Asian modal scales, West African harp traditions, and Nordic choral texture, layered with a precision that would take a human arranger years to achieve.

The second movement, 'Suspension,' runs twenty-two minutes and is built around a single melodic fragment that transforms through forty-seven variations, each one microscopically different, each one audible in full only to listeners with high-grade augmentation. The third movement, 'Weight,' is the suite's emotional center — a spare, almost hymn-like piece for voice and strings that has been described as the most purely human-feeling music on the album, which critics have noted is either ironic or the point. The fourth movement, 'Return,' ends in a seven-minute fade that in neural-feed mode delivers a tactile sensation of descent.
creator: Maren Solís-Ekwueme
audience: Tier 4 corporate professionals, Tier 5 Spire residents, classical music patrons, augmentation-culture elites
cultural_impact: The album became a flashpoint in the ongoing argument about AI authorship and cultural gatekeeping. When a bootleg version reached Tier 2 feeds six months after release, the response split along predictable lines: Spire commentators were outraged at the 'degraded experience' of hearing it on black-market hardware; Circuit and Shelf listeners were outraged that it had been kept from them in the first place. Maren Solís-Ekwueme gave one interview in which she said she had wanted the suite to be released at all tiers simultaneously and had been overruled by the Endowment — the interview was quietly removed from Vantablack's media archive within a week. The album won three Vantablack Cultural Awards and is considered the definitive example of the AI-collaboration genre, for better or worse.
known_fans: bootleg distributors who consider access a political act
story_hooks: Maren Solís-Ekwueme has disappeared from public life since the interview removal — someone wants to find her, and the Vantablack Endowment would very much prefer they didn't.

The AXIOM-7 AI system used to compose the suite has been quietly decommissioned; a data broker claims to have a copy of the system's full compositional logs, which might reveal something Vantablack doesn't want known about how the music was actually made.

A Tier 1 hardware collective has built a rig capable of delivering the full neural-feed experience on salvaged implants and is planning a free public listening event — Vantablack's enforcement team has been notified.
